body_markdown:
Chances are good that if you live in a neighborhood of single-family homes, one or more of your neighbors has a[Little Free Library](https://littlefreelibrary.org/) . It’s not just an American phenomenon, either. There are now more than 200,000 tiny book exchanges with their “Take a book, share a book” ethos in 85 countries around the globe. One house, though, in suburban Detroit’s Huntington Woods, has two little share boxes out front. One, *Ms. Joyce’s Library* , is an actual Little Free Library. Not far from *Ms. Joyce’s Library* is another small box, this one in the iconic blue-and-orange “Gulf Oil” racing livery, with professional automotive pinstriping and lettering proclaiming *Jim’s Garage* . Seeing it, you’d probably guess that it has something to do with cars, and you’d be correct. In fact, it’s full of little cars; the little garage is engineer and car enthusiast Jim Krom’s way of creating a new generation of car guys and gals. He wants kids to know that “cars are cool.”


[Ronnie Schreiber](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/rschreiber/)


*Jim’s Garage* opened for “business” on New Year’s Day 2026, filled with 70 of Jim’s favorite little cars: Hot Wheels. One week later, more than half had been replaced with other scale models. “Most of these are not the ones I stocked it with,” Krom told the Detroit Free Press. Not all of the replacements are 1:64 scale Hot Wheels and similar die-cast models. Some are larger, like in the displays you’d see in a grocery or drug store. When we visited *Jim’s Garage,* there was an even larger toy Jeep left at the base of the little garage’s sturdy pedestal. The result is an eclectic collection of model cars and trucks with something sure to interest both novice and longtime car buffs.


[Ronnie Schreiber](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/rschreiber/)


[Ronnie Schreiber](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/rschreiber/)


[Ronnie Schreiber](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/rschreiber/)


Krom, 54, is one of those people with gasoline in their veins, a big car guy. A third-generation engineer, Krom is a manufacturing engineer with Auburn Hills automotive supplier Voltava. As a kid, while his parents raced at the Waterford Hills road course, he and the other racers’ kids would have their own competitions with Hot Wheels. He still heads straight to aisle F-3 when he’s at the Meijer store on Eight Mile in Detroit “I always go to the Hot Wheels aisle,” he says. His favorites are those that he calls “actual cars,” not the wild customs that Hot Wheels can be known for. He also is pretty grounded, opening up the blister packs and treating them as toys, not just precious collectibles. “There’s a meme that goes, ‘The world’s most expensive hobby starts at 99 cents,’ ” Krom told the Freep (the Detroit Free Press) not long after setting up Jim’s Garage.


[Ronnie Schreiber](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/rschreiber/)


The little garage is not a completely original idea. Krom was inspired by his wife Joyce’s little book library, and a few similar lending garages he found online. Taking care of her little lending library is a bit of a busman’s holiday, as she’s a manager in the Detroit Public Library system in her day job.


[Ronnie Schreiber](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/rschreiber/)


Jim thought the little garages that he found online were too small, though, so he made his little garage a little bigger: 18″ high by 18″ wide by 12″ deep out of spare pine lumber, and gave the little parking structure three levels, with the shelves striped yellow just like in real parking lots. The garage door, emblazoned with “Take A Car Leave A Car,” has clear acrylic panels so you can see inside when it’s closed. The door is hinged at the top and secured by strong magnets when it is open, to protect little hands.


Krom doesn’t just play with little cars. In addition to family daily drivers, he has a show-quality ’49 Cadillac, an ’85 Chevy C-10 pickup, a ’55 Chevy Bel Air, a long-term ’64 Corvette project, and a couple of VW Bugs.


[Ronnie Schreiber](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/rschreiber/)


Krom told the Freep that he’s thinking of constructing another little garage and giving it away. He’d like to see the idea catch on as a way of bringing more young people into the car hobby. “The baby boomers are aging out of car culture,” he said, hoping to engage their grandkids with *Jim’s Garage.*
